question.text: Under the PFUTP Regulations, 'mis-selling' of securities includes which of the following?

answer.text: Knowingly making false statements, concealing material facts or associated risks, and not taking reasonable care to ensure suitability
Only not taking reasonable care to ensure suitability
Only knowingly concealing material facts and associated risks
Only knowingly making a false or misleading statement

explanation.text: The Logic: The PFUTP Regulations define mis-selling as the sale of securities by: (i) knowingly making a false or misleading statement, (ii) knowingly concealing or omitting material facts of the scheme/securities, (iii) knowingly concealing the associated risk factors, or (iv) not taking reasonable care to ensure suitability of the scheme/securities to the buyer. The Trap: Options B, C, and D each capture only part of the definition; mis-selling under the regulation requires the full four-limb description, so the partial-only options are incorrect. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-III-A workbook (Dec 2025), page 146, which lists the four mis-selling limbs.
